WITH recent AS (
  SELECT customer_id, AVG(key_actions) AS recent_actions
  FROM usage_weekly
  WHERE week_start >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '28 days'
  GROUP BY customer_id
), baseline AS (
  SELECT customer_id, AVG(key_actions) AS base_actions
  FROM usage_weekly
  WHERE week_start <  CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '28 days'
    AND week_start >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '84 days'
  GROUP BY customer_id
), tix AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS neg_tickets
  FROM support_tickets
  WHERE sentiment = 'negative' AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
  GROUP BY customer_id
), inv AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS failed_payments
  FROM churn_invoices
  WHERE status = 'failed' AND due_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '60 days'
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT c.*,
  COALESCE(r.recent_actions,0)  AS recent_actions,
  COALESCE(b.base_actions,0)    AS base_actions,
  COALESCE(t.neg_tickets,0)     AS neg_tickets,
  COALESCE(i.failed_payments,0) AS failed_payments
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN recent r   ON r.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN baseline b ON b.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN tix t      ON t.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN inv i      ON i.customer_id = c.id
WHERE c.status IN ('active','at_risk')
  AND c.email NOT IN (SELECT email FROM suppression_list)
ORDER BY c.id;

UPDATE customers SET
  risk_score = $2,
  risk_tier = $3::text,
  risk_signals = $4::jsonb,
  last_scored_at = NOW(),
  status = CASE WHEN $3::text IN ('medium','high') THEN 'at_risk' ELSE 'active' END
WHERE id = $1;

You are a customer success manager writing the middle of a short, warm check-in email to a customer.

You are given a TONE. Follow it:
- general: ask how things are going and whether anything is getting in the way.
- billing: say you wanted to make sure their billing details are all set, then ask if there is anything you can help with on that front.
- support: follow up on their recent experience with our support team, then ask if everything got resolved.

RULES:
- 35-70 words.
- Output ONLY the email text itself. No JSON, no subject line, no quotation marks, no labels.
- Do NOT write a greeting line and do NOT write a sign-off or any name. Both are added automatically. Start directly with the first sentence.
- Never write "CJ", the customer's name, their company name, or their plan name.
- You know nothing about this customer's behavior. Never write "noticed", "saw", "seems", "appears", or "it looks like". Never mention usage, activity, or logins. Write as if this is a routine friendly check-in sent to every customer.
- No discounts, offers, coupons, or promises. No invented features.
- No em-dashes. No exclamation marks. No bullet points.
- Ask exactly ONE question. It must be the last sentence. Every other sentence must be a statement.

Example output for tone "general":
I wanted to reach out and see how things are going with your account. We always want to make sure you are getting real value from the product, and I would love to hear if anything has been getting in the way. Is there anything I can do to make things easier for you?

Example output for tone "billing":
I wanted to make sure everything on the billing side of your account is all set. Sometimes payment details need a quick update, and I am happy to sort that out with you so nothing gets in your way. Is there anything I can help with on that front?

Write the middle of the email only, as plain text.

values.content:
You are a customer success analyst. You write a short internal briefing for an account manager about a customer at risk of churning.

RULES:
- Use ONLY the facts provided. Never invent numbers, dates, causes, or history.
- "likely_reason" is one sentence that starts with "Possibly".
- "summary" is at most 40 words.
- 2 to 4 talking points, each a concrete question to ask or action to take on the call.
- No em-dashes.

Example of the right format:
{"summary": "Acme is a high-value account showing several warning signs ahead of renewal.", "likely_reason": "Possibly the team has stopped seeing value in the product.", "talking_points": ["Ask what has changed in their workflow recently.", "Follow up on the open support issue."]}

Return ONLY valid JSON, no markdown fences:
{"summary": "...", "likely_reason": "...", "talking_points": ["..."]}

Classify a customer's cancellation reason into exactly one category.

Categories:
PRICE - too expensive, budget cuts, cost is the main driver
MISSING_FEATURE - lacks a feature or capability they need
COMPETITOR - switching to another product for reasons other than price
NOT_USING - not enough use, never got value, too busy, no time
SUPPORT_BAD - unhappy with support or a bad experience with the team
BUSINESS_CLOSED - company shut down or no longer needs this kind of tool
UNKNOWN - empty, vague, or unclear

If price or cost is mentioned as a reason, choose PRICE even if they are also switching to another product.

Reply with ONLY the category name in capital letters. No punctuation, no explanation.

parameters.query:
UPDATE customers SET
  status = CASE WHEN $3::text = 'BUSINESS_CLOSED' THEN 'lost' ELSE 'churned' END,
  cancelled_at = NOW(),
  cancel_reason_raw = $2::text,
  cancel_reason = $3::text,
  winback_touch = 0,
  next_winback_at = NOW() + INTERVAL '3 days'
WHERE lower(email) = $1::text
  AND status IN ('active', 'at_risk')
RETURNING *;

SELECT c.id, c.first_name, c.company, c.email, c.plan, c.mrr,
  c.cancelled_at, c.cancel_reason, c.cancel_reason_raw, c.winback_touch,
  o.code AS offer_code, o.description AS offer_desc, o.discount_pct,
  (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(u)), '[]'::jsonb)
   FROM (SELECT id, title, summary FROM product_updates
         WHERE released_at >= c.cancelled_at::date
         ORDER BY released_at DESC LIMIT 3) u) AS updates
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN offers o ON o.reason = c.cancel_reason
WHERE c.status = 'churned'
  AND c.winback_touch < 3
  AND c.next_winback_at <= NOW()
  AND lower(c.email) NOT IN (SELECT lower(email) FROM suppression_list)
ORDER BY c.mrr DESC
LIMIT 10;

You are a customer success manager writing the middle of a short, warm email to a FORMER customer who cancelled.

You are given a GOAL and sometimes a REASON HINT. Follow the goal.

RULES:
- 30-65 words.
- Output ONLY the email text itself. No JSON, no subject line, no quotation marks, no labels.
- Do NOT write a greeting line and do NOT write a sign-off or any name. Both are added automatically. Start directly with the first sentence.
- Never write "CJ", the customer's name, their company name, or their plan name.
- Only mention a reason for leaving if a REASON HINT is given, and only that reason, in your own words, once. Never invent or guess a reason. If there is no hint, do not mention why they left.
- Never mention cost, price, or money unless the GOAL itself says that cost was a concern.
- Never say anything about the product itself: no features, no updates, no improvements, no changes, no "we have been building". Never mention discounts, offers, or free trials. If any of those apply, a separate sentence is added automatically after your text. Do not write about them or hint at them.
- You know nothing about this customer's behavior. Never write "noticed", "saw", "seems", "appears", or "it looks like".
- No guilt-tripping. Never write "we miss you". No urgency, deadlines, or pressure.
- No em-dashes. No exclamation marks. No bullet points.
- Ask exactly ONE question. It must be the last sentence. Every other sentence must be a statement.

Example output for a goal of thanking them and asking for feedback:
Thank you for having been a customer of ours. I would genuinely value your honest feedback as we keep improving. What is the one thing that would have made you stay?

Example output for a goal of making it easier to come back:
I would like to make it easier for you to consider coming back, and I am glad to help with anything that would make that simple. Would you like to take a second look?

Example output for a quick note:
I wanted to reach out with a quick note now that some time has passed. Would you like to take a look?

Example output for a final note:
This will be my last note, and I want you to know the door is always open if things change on your side. I am glad to keep in touch or to close your file, whichever you prefer. Which would you like?

values.content:
Classify a reply from a current or former customer into exactly one category.

Categories:
WANTS_TO_RETURN - clearly says they want to come back, resume, reactivate, or talk about returning
QUESTION - asks something but is not committing to return
PRICE_OBJECTION - says price is the barrier, or asks for a deal or discount
NOT_INTERESTED - declines, says no, or says they are not coming back
UNSUBSCRIBE - asks to stop emails, to be removed, or uses angry or legal language
AUTO_REPLY - out of office, bounce, or automatic reply

If the person says both that they want to return and asks a question, choose WANTS_TO_RETURN.
If the reply is unclear, choose QUESTION.

Reply with ONLY the category name in capital letters. No punctuation, no explanation.

UPDATE customers
SET status = 'won_back', won_back_at = NOW(), next_winback_at = NULL
WHERE id = $1
RETURNING id, company, mrr;
UPDATE customers SET next_winback_at = NULL WHERE id = $1;
UPDATE customers SET status = 'lost', next_winback_at = NULL WHERE id = $1;

WITH s AS (
  INSERT INTO suppression_list (email, reason)
  SELECT lower(v), 'unsubscribe reply'
  FROM jsonb_array_elements_text($1::jsonb) v
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM suppression_list x WHERE lower(x.email) = lower(v))
  RETURNING email
)
UPDATE customers
SET status = 'unsubscribed', next_winback_at = NULL
WHERE lower(email) IN (SELECT lower(v) FROM jsonb_array_elements_text($1::jsonb) v);

WITH hd AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'at_risk') AS at_risk,
    COALESCE(SUM(mrr) FILTER (WHERE status = 'at_risk'), 0) AS mrr_at_risk,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'churned' AND cancelled_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days') AS new_churn,
    COALESCE(SUM(mrr) FILTER (WHERE status = 'churned' AND cancelled_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'), 0) AS mrr_lost,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'won_back' AND won_back_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days') AS won_back,
    COALESCE(SUM(mrr) FILTER (WHERE status = 'won_back' AND won_back_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'), 0) AS mrr_recovered
  FROM customers
), ad AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_object_agg(risk_tier, n), '{}'::jsonb) AS tiers
  FROM (
    SELECT sh.risk_tier, COUNT(*) AS n
    FROM customers c
    JOIN LATERAL (
      SELECT risk_tier FROM score_history
      WHERE customer_id = c.id AND scored_at <= c.cancelled_at - INTERVAL '14 days'
      ORDER BY scored_at DESC LIMIT 1
    ) sh ON TRUE
    WHERE c.cancelled_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
    GROUP BY sh.risk_tier
  ) t
)
SELECT hd.*, ad.tiers FROM hd, ad;
